title: One owned thing: omitting meidän and teidän
focus: Omit meidän or teidän while retaining the ending; keep heidän in identification sentences.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Write “This is your book.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Address a group. Leave out teidän; keep the noun ending. Use kirja (“book”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nne identifies your ownership. Teidän can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.targetSkill: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
kirja (“book”) + -nne = kirjanne. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one. The ending identifies the owner, so teidän can be left out.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Meidän is the personal owner form of me; it selects -mme.
kissa (“cat”) + -mme = kissamme. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -mme: use kissamme.
Keep the possessive ending -mme even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Meidän needs -mme; changing the ending changes the owner.
